new_statements.quote: Sur le plan prosodique, le kotafon comporte des tons distinctifs, tandis que l'allemand possède des accents qui ne sont distinctifs que dans peu de cas. (p. 15) [...] L'allemand fait partie des langues à intonations, comme d'ailleurs la plupart des langues européennes, Meibauer (2007: 104). Dans ces langues, il n'existe pas de tons, mais des accents. (p. 31) [...] En matière d'éléments suprasegmentaux, nous avons constaté que les deux langues ont peu de points communs, mais assez de différences. En effet, en kotafon, nous avons divers tons: les tons ponctuels [...] et les tons modulés [...] qui ont une fonction distinctive. [...] En allemand, on a plutôt des accents (p. 36)
new_statements.translation: On the prosodic level, Kotafon has distinctive tones, whereas German has accents that are distinctive only in a few cases. (p. 15) [...] German belongs to the intonation languages, like most European languages (Meibauer 2007: 104). In these languages there are no tones, but accents. (p. 31) [...] As regards suprasegmental elements, we found that the two languages have few points in common but plenty of differences. Indeed, in Kotafon we have various tones: the level tones [...] and the contour tones [...] which have a distinctive function. [...] In German one has accents instead (p. 36)
new_statements.citation: Degbevi, Comlan Athanase & Flavien Gbeto. 2017. Analyse contrastive des systèmes phonético-phonologiques du kotafon et de l'allemand. Revue du CAMES, Littérature, langues et linguistique 5 (1er semestre 2017): 15-38. Université d'Abomey-Calavi.
new_statements.locator: Résumé, p. 15 (pdf p. 1); sec. 4.2.5 'Distribution des accents en allemand', p. 31 (pdf p. 17); sec. 5.4 'Au niveau des éléments prosodiques', p. 36 (pdf p. 22)
new_statements.check: confirmed by a second reader, with minor differences
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: File opened: (24 pp., text layer present, Nitro Pro 2017; journal pp. 15-38, pdf page = journal page - 14). All three quoted passages are present verbatim: (1) Resume, journal p. 15 / pdf p. 1: "Sur le plan prosodique, le kotafon comporte des tons distinctifs, tandis que l'allemand possede des accents qui ne sont distinctifs que dans peu de cas." (2) sec. 4.2.5 "Distribution des accents en allemand": "L'allemand fait partie des langues a intonations, comme d'ailleurs la plupart des langues europeennes, Meibauer (2007: 104). Dans ces langues, il n'existe pas de tons, mais des accents." -- but this is on journal p. 32 / pdf p. 18, not p. 31 / pdf p. 17 as the report's locator says. (3) sec. 5…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Kotafon is a tone language with two tonemes (H, L) and derived M, LH, HL, MH, HM; word-level prosody is tonal. The only accent statement is contrastive: the authors set Kotafon's distinctive tones against German's word accent (initial-syllable stress) as the main suprasegmental difference, implying Kotafon has no word stress of the German type. No stress position is stated for Kotafon.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed for Kotafon (secondary accent mentioned only for German compounds, p. 32).
new_statements.exceptions: Gbeto 2006 (p. 88) calls the fixed HB melody imposed on reduplicated verb stems with voiced initial consonant an 'accentual phenomenon' interpretation, and (p. 103) says contour tones occur only word-finally and so serve a demarcative function; Capo 1991 (p. 22, per Google Books snippet) notes English loanwords with stressed final syllable take a falling tone in Gbe.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level tone (nouns, verbs, imperatives, reduplicated verbs); the tone-vs-accent contrast is stated for the languages as wholes. Field data from Mono department (Lokossa area); Gbeto 2006 describes the Tozoumê (Lokossa) variety.
new_statements.first_reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.identity_note: Kotafon = CNL 1983 'kogbe'; Glottolog kota1272 is language-level with no dialects. Gbeto 2006 describes the variety of Tozoumê (Lokossa); Degbevi & Gbeto 2017 draw on Mono-department field data (two arrondissements plus Lokossa town). Two of three Ci Gbe (cigb1235) communities also call their speech 'Kotafon' (Henson 2011,../cigb1235), but the sources above concern Kotafon proper.

sources.note: Prosodic comparison: Kotafon has distinctive tones (B, H, M, BH, HB; sec. 4.1.5 p. 23), German has word accents (sec. 4.2.5 p. 31, 'Dans ces langues [à intonations], il n'existe pas de tons, mais des accents'); abstract p. 15 and sec. 5.4 p. 36 oppose Kotafon tone to German accent as the main suprasegmental difference. No stress position for Kotafon; no explicit 'no stress' sentence.

sources.note: Tonology of the Tozoumê (Lokossa) variety: two underlying tones H and B, M/BH/HB/MH/HM derived, voiceless obstruents insert H. 'stress' 0 hits; 'accent' only p. 88 (HB melody in verbal reduplication = 'interprétation d'un phénomène accentuel') and as diacritic names; p. 103: contour tones appear only in final position and so have 'une fonction démarcative'. No word-stress statement.
fr: 32 consonants, 12 vowels (5 nasal), tonal; bibliography names Gbeto 2006, Hatfield & McHenry 2011, Degbevi & Gbeto 2017 (the lead to the CAMES article). en: stub. Nothing on stress.
